evidence: Every reviews_handler fixture used state CHANGES_REQUESTED, so nothing exercised _BOT_REVIEWS_JQ dropping its state filter; f5c5038 added a COMMENTED fixture and a real-jq run. The same commit also introduced the defects found later as F5 and F14.
guidance_note: When a refactor's defining change is removing a filter, add a fixture of the newly admitted shape in the same commit as the refactor.

evidence: The packet does not show GitHub's review schema, and the reviewer itself says it is 'not fully certain GitHub's reviews API ever returns a null body'. The pushback holds either way: a None reaching parse_agent_artifact crashes loudly and can never report an unreviewed head as clean, while the suggested isinstance guard would silently turn it into 'not an artifact'.
The `wait` help said 'nonzero exit unless conclusion is success' while cmd_wait gained an `elif not result["reviewed"]` failure branch; f5c5038 updated the help string.
guidance_note: When adding a new failure branch to a CLI subcommand, update its argparse help in the same edit.

evidence: This duplicates F2 on the same line and round, and the reviewer again hedges about whether null ever occurs. The proposed `(body or "").rstrip()` would launder an impossible value into 'no-review-for-head', whereas the unguarded code fails loudly in the safe direction.

f5c5038 added `check("jq is installed", ...)` followed by an unconditional `real_subprocess.run(["jq", ...], check=True)`. A missing jq therefore raises FileNotFoundError and aborts every later check in the file, which contradicts the F1 reply's claim that 'jq absence fails loudly' as one check. 193a478 moved the call behind check_returns.
guidance_note: When a new test step can raise, route it through the file's existing check_returns/check_raises harness rather than a bare call next to a non-gating check.

evidence: Flag false positive: the adversarial_provider.wait `reviewed: True` addition was in the original diff (round 0's adversarial-provider scope), and f5c5038 touched only the bin/review help and github_threads tests. The missing test was real, and 193a478 added adversarial_provider.test.py.
guidance_note: When a contract field is added to every provider, add a contract test for each provider, not only the primary one.

evidence: Flag false positive: cmd_wait's two-branch halt logic was in the original diff, and f5c5038 changed only its help text. No test drove cmd_wait, and 193a478 added review_cli.test.py covering all three shapes.
guidance_note: The enforcement point a feature exists for (here cmd_wait's halt) needs its own test in the original PR.

evidence: Flag false positive: the closed union `None | "round-cap" | "fork" | "no-review-for-head"` was in the original PROVIDER_CONTRACT diff, and f5c5038 did not touch that file. NOT_REVIEWED_MARKER_RE `([a-z-]+)` passes any reason through, so the documented type was false. 193a478 retyped it as `None | str`.
guidance_note: When documenting a field filled by a regex capture, derive the documented type from the regex, not from today's known values.

evidence: The cross-endpoint read-after-write assumption exists, but createReview has returned before the run can complete. A stale read fails in the safe direction ('halts with sha + run URL ... can never merge an unreviewed head'), and the reviewer's retry-with-backoff only makes a stale read rarer.

Flag false positive: the stale 'a User can't even post CHANGES_REQUESTED on their own PR' justification was carried over in the original bot_reviews refactor, and 193a478 did not touch github_threads.py. The reasoning no longer fit the all-states set, and a2a56bf rescoped the comment.
guidance_note: When widening a filter, re-read the comment that justified the narrow filter and restate only what holds for the wider set.

evidence: Flag false positive: a2a56bf touched only github_threads.py. The v0.3.0 CHANGELOG entry was release metadata written during review, not the fix for any finding. Its test bullet listed the fix-added suites but omitted action_provider.test.py, and 25de2ef added it.
guidance_note: Write release-note test bullets from the full list of test files the PR touches, not from memory of the latest fixes.

evidence: Flag false positive: the text 'implement wait as a no-op that returns ... reviewed: True ... verifying its own review exists IS the proof' is in the original PR's contract diff, and a2a56bf did not touch it. The text contradicts itself and contradicts the PR's purpose. 25de2ef replaced it with 'reviewed: True is never a constant'.
guidance_note: When a PR exists to stop a hardcoded success, search its own docs and stubs for templates that still tell implementers to hardcode it.

evidence: 25de2ef, the F12 fix, rewrote the synchronous arm of local_provider's NotImplementedError to require proof. It left the async arm as bare 'poll for completion', which is exactly where a round-capped run completes green. ab6d418 extended the async arm.
guidance_note: When rewriting guidance to enforce a new invariant, apply it to every branch of that guidance (sync and async), not just the branch the finding quoted.

evidence: f5c5038, the F1 fix, inserted `gt.bot_reviews(PR)` before `change_requests(PR)` on the same fake. The surviving 'change_requests: asks gh to walk every page' check on `fake.calls[0]` then inspected bot_reviews' call instead. 25de2ef (the flagged commit) did not cause this, and ab6d418 checked calls[1].
guidance_note: When inserting a new call ahead of existing assertions on a shared fake's call log, re-index or re-scope every positional assertion that follows.

evidence: Flag false positive: the 'existence check IS the proof' comment and the unanchored `MARKER_RE.search` both predate 25de2ef (the comment appears in F6's round-1 hunk). The gap was real, since action_provider anchors its markers and adversarial did not. ab6d418 anchored the regex with a test, and the agent declined author scoping with a stated threat distinction.
guidance_note: When two sibling providers parse their own markers, give them the same anchoring rule and the same 'quoted mid-body' test in the original PR.

narrative: The PR adds a reviewed/not_reviewed_reason verdict to every provider's wait(). Most findings were pre-existing gaps in the original diff surfaced across rounds 1-4: missing tests for adversarial wait and cmd_wait, a closed-union doc type, a self-contradicting 'no-op' template, and an unanchored marker. Three were fix-caused: the F1 test fix both left the jq call ungated (F5) and mis-pointed an existing call-log assertion (F14), and the F12 doc fix left the async arm unfixed (F13). Each round also carried at least one non-fix-caused finding, so no round is attributable purely to bad fixes. The sixth push hit the round cap, and the agent hand-reviewed the 25-line unreviewed delta before merging.
guidance_observations: The original PR shipped a contract change across three providers with tests for only one; the reviewer then drip-fed the missing per-provider tests over two rounds.
Two of the three fix-caused findings came from one test-fix commit (f5c5038), which suggests running and re-reading the whole test file after editing a shared fixture.
Pushbacks on the null-body and temporal-coupling findings were argued from failure direction (loud crash or safe halt), which held up.

evidence: Flag false positive: 8193f26 changed only README.md, and the test file's mechanical rename was in the original diff. No case wrote `context_ceiling = ...`. 35b006a added one, and the agent showed it was the sole failure under three alias-readmitting mutants.
guidance_note: When renaming a config key with a 'fails like any unknown key' contract, add a test that writes the old key and asserts refusal; the agent's own reply cites the v0.4.0 precedent for exactly this.

narrative: The PR renamed the context_ceiling setting to ceiling. Round 0's only finding was out-of-diff: a README tag example naming the now-stale 0.4.0. The agent fixed it by deleting the version copy rather than bumping it. Round 1 found the missing old-key refusal test, which was present in the original diff and not caused by the README fix. The agent also noticed that the review loop's fetch reads only threads, so out-of-diff findings would have been silently dropped, and filed a ticket for it.
guidance_observations: The agent answered an out-of-diff finding by removing the duplicated fact rather than re-syncing it, which prevents the identical finding next release.
Mutation-testing the new check before claiming it bites was the right evidence bar.

evidence: _our_review_for re-implemented the `gh api --paginate` plus per-page `--jq` JSONL read that github_threads.bot_reviews already had. The agent extracted `github_threads.paginated(endpoint, jq)` for both callers and correctly noted that bot_reviews itself could not serve, because the adversarial review posts as a User.
guidance_note: Before writing a paginated gh/jq reader, grep the shared github_threads module for an existing one and extend it.

narrative: The PR made the adversarial provider read every page of reviews. The single finding was duplication of the pagination technique already in github_threads. The agent extracted a shared helper, mutation-checked it, and round 1 approved.
guidance_observations: One round could have been saved by reusing the existing primitive in the original change.

evidence: EXIT_HINT spells out 'run ExitWorktree with action "keep"' as literal text beside `PERMITTED_EXIT = {"ExitWorktree": "keep"}`, and the comment above EXIT_HINT itself claims [LAW:one-source-of-truth]. The thread got no reply, and the PR merged with it unresolved.
guidance_note: When a hint string names a permitted value, interpolate it from the constant that decides permission, especially when the comment claims one-source-of-truth.

evidence: Flag false positive: c255b9b changed only .github/workflows/code-review.yml, the generated reviewer template. This is the reviewer re-raising the unaddressed F1, not a defect introduced by a fix, and it too was left unanswered at merge.

Flag false positive: c255b9b touched only the workflow file, and the ExitWorktree tests were in the original diff. The suite covers 'a permitted call that is not the launcher does not count as the close-out' for other permitted calls but has no Stop-side case for ExitWorktree keep. No reply was posted before merge.
guidance_note: When adding a new permitted-but-not-closeout call, add the Stop-side 'does not count as close-out' case the suite already uses for its siblings.

narrative: The PR permits ExitWorktree keep so a worktree session can reach its close-out. Both review rounds were CHANGES_REQUESTED. The round 0 finding (EXIT_HINT duplicating PERMITTED_EXIT) got no reply, round 1 re-raised it and added a missing Stop-side test, and the PR merged with all three threads unresolved and unanswered. The only post-review commit was a regenerated code-review.yml, unrelated to any finding.
guidance_observations: The PR merged over two CHANGES_REQUESTED reviews with zero replies on any thread, skipping the address-pr-reviews loop entirely.
Round 1 exists only because a generated-workflow push re-triggered review, and it repeated the unanswered round 0 finding.
